question: How do path speed, chirp frequency and path sampling resolution affect Ca_HVA gate prediction with frozen primitives?
nonredundancy: Task 6 already tested an eight-sample ramp. Task 8 uses forty 0.025 ms substeps, independently varied ramp speed and chirp frequency, plus paired start-only/coarse/fine path information controls.

source.teacher: canonical compiled Ca_HVA.mod, NEURON isolated-gate oracle

arms: exact formula with full fine path as target
physical-tau each seed with V_start only
physical-tau each seed with coarse path
physical-tau each seed with full fine path

contrasts.path_information: Exact formula start-only and coarse-path errors against exact fine-path target isolate missing temporal information.
contrasts.representation: LUT and each physical-tau seed are compared only within the same path view.
contrasts.speed_frequency: Report the four families separately; do not conceal high-frequency failure in an aggregate.

preflight: Authentic NEURON pilot must match extracted formula within 1e-9 gate occupancy; no pilot failure can be interpreted as candidate error.
freeze_policy: No candidate retraining or selection. Save development report and freeze before generating sealed paths; sealed outcomes are descriptive and cannot alter arms, thresholds or seed choice.
interpretation_limit: Exogenous future voltage path is an oracle input for diagnostics, not an available input to an endogenous closed-loop predictor. No 642-segment, dynamic-calcium or learned-voltage-updater claim.
